The introduced change calls `record_episode(self.client, state["messages"][-2:], source="langgraph")` in the middleware's after_model hook to persist every turn automatically.

From the Vinc graph on framework integration packages (concept:doc.vinc.plan.framework-integration-packages-2026-09-28) and LangGraph explicit writes (record:2026-09-29-vin188-langgraph-compatibility), these integration packages are designed to read the graph state continuously but write only on explicit, deliberate calls rather than every turn. The write involves posting a structured Episode with metadata and about edges, typically triggered by user action or explicit logic, to avoid noise and unfiltered writes to the graph that may degrade graph quality or cause unintended side effects.

This automatic persistent write on every turn via middleware risks over-writing or flooding the graph with incomplete or irrelevant turns, against the intended pattern. The prior `after_model` returning None was intentional to separate reads (cheap, continuous) from writes (explicit, careful). Hence, this diff contradicts the expected design of deliberate, explicit graph writing in Vinc framework integration packages.

Verdict: This diff introduces over-engineering and is incorrect per the Vinc framework integration package principles. It should be deleted or reverted to return None without automatic writes.
